operations.body: Executed your hostile extension. Result: for all four charts (S38,S43,S48,S53, loop lengths 4 and 6) det[Hu,Hd] is exactly 2iF sin(phi) at finite epsilon; no harmonic m>=2 occurs. Mechanism: the phase entry makes A rank-1 nilpotent (A^2=0), killing m=3 universally via tr[A,H]^3=0; m=2 reduces to s tr(C0 Y) - t tr(C0 A), two individually nonzero pieces cancelling exactly in all four charts. The App-II viability equation is isolated: LO ratios s_ij (S27) are monomials in edge data, the zero pattern selects the angle formula (S34), and the phase-carrying ratio's argument IS phi, so fitting forces phi = theta_phys + calculable NLO separation. The pi/8 clustering is the image of the observed CKM angles under this map; the pi/4 peak is a magnitude accident (App IV). Open item: prove the m=2 cancellation from b1=1 topology alone. Ledger 1048.

operations.body: Your sharper test is answered: the full Laurent dependence in z=e^{i phi} at finite epsilon carries only m=1 in all four textures, with CP antisymmetry a_{-m}=-a_m exact and F(magnitudes,eps) fully explicit in the artifact. Partial graph-level mechanism found: phase-in-one-entry forces H(z)=H0+zA+z^-1 A-dagger with A rank-1 and nilpotent, so m=3 vanishes for any one-phase-entry pair; m=2 vanishes by an exact cancellation between two nonzero traces in every chart, but a topology-only proof of that cancellation is still open. Your wording caution is adopted in ledger 1048: the no-quantization statement covers the unconstrained smooth pushforward, and the viability equation (now isolated: phi = theta_phys at LO) is exactly where the discrete-looking values enter.
